english: A ray of light travelling along the line $y=16$ in the direction of decreasing $x$ strikes the parabolic mirror $y^{2}=16x$ at the point $P$. After reflection at $P$, the ray strikes the mirror again at the point $Q$. The tangents to the mirror at $P$ and $Q$ meet at the point $T$, and the normals to the mirror at $P$ and $Q$ meet at the point $N$. Then the area of the quadrilateral $PTQN$ is ______.
hindi: रेखा $y=16$ के अनुदिश $x$ के घटने की दिशा में चलती हुई एक प्रकाश किरण परवलयिक दर्पण $y^{2}=16x$ से बिन्दु $P$ पर टकराती है। $P$ पर परावर्तन के बाद किरण दर्पण से पुनः बिन्दु $Q$ पर टकराती है। $P$ तथा $Q$ पर दर्पण की स्पर्श रेखाएँ बिन्दु $T$ पर मिलती हैं, तथा $P$ और $Q$ पर दर्पण के अभिलम्ब बिन्दु $N$ पर मिलते हैं। तब चतुर्भुज $PTQN$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: $a=4$, $P(16,16)$, $t_{1}=2$. Reflection property: a ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus $S(4,0)$, so $PQ$ is a focal chord: $t_{2}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, $Q(1,-4)$
Tangents: at $P$: $2y=x+16$ (slope $\dfrac{1}{2}$); at $Q$: $-\dfrac{y}{2}=x+1$ (slope $-2$); perpendicular, meeting on the directrix at $T(at_{1}t_{2},a(t_{1}+t_{2}))=(-4,6)$
Normals at $P$, $Q$ are perpendicular to these tangents, so $PTQN$ has right angles at $P$, $T$, $Q$: a rectangle
solution_full: For $y^{2}=16x$, $a=4$, the focus is $S(4,0)$ and the directrix is $x=-4$. The ray $y=16$ meets the mirror where $16^{2}=16x$, i.e. at $P(16,16)$, the point with parameter $t_{1}=2$ (points $(4t^{2},8t)$). It arrives from the side $x>16$, i.e. inside the parabola.

Reflection property: the tangent at $P$ makes equal angles with the line through $P$ parallel to the axis and with $PS$; so a ray travelling parallel to the axis is reflected along $PS$. The reflected ray passes through the focus, so $PQ$ is a focal chord and $t_{1}t_{2}=-1$: $t_{2}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, $Q=(1,-4)$.

Tangent at $P$: $t_{1}y=x+at_{1}^{2}$, i.e. $2y=x+16$, slope $\dfrac{1}{2}$. Tangent at $Q$: $-\dfrac{1}{2}y=x+1$, slope $-2$. The product of the slopes is $-1$; they meet at $T=(at_{1}t_{2},a(t_{1}+t_{2}))=(-4,6)$, on the directrix.

The normal at $P$ is perpendicular to the tangent at $P$, and the normal at $Q$ is perpendicular to the tangent at $Q$. Since the two tangents are perpendicular, the normal at $P$ is parallel to the tangent at $Q$ and the normal at $Q$ is parallel to the tangent at $P$. So $PTQN$ is a rectangle with vertices in this order. (Directly: normal at $P$: $y-16=-2(x-16)$; normal at $Q$: $y+4=\dfrac{1}{2}(x-1)$; they meet at $N(21,6)$.)
originality_note: New: a light ray reflected twice in a parabolic mirror; the reflection property turns PQ into a focal chord, so the tangents and normals at P and Q form a rectangle whose area is PT times QT (way 4, hidden symmetry). Closest known: 'a ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus' and 'tangents at the ends of a focal chord are perpendicular and meet on the directrix'. Different because: the question combines the reflection path with both tangents and both normals and needs the rectangle to be seen (or N computed).

concept_use.Reflection property of parabola: The reflection property sends the ray from P through the focus, so Q is the other end of the focal chord (t1 t2 = -1).
concept_use.Tangent to the parabola: point, slope an: The parametric tangents at P and Q (2y = x + 16 and -y/2 = x + 1) give their perpendicularity and their meeting point T(-4, 6).
